verdict_changes.reason: Notification is commonly a concurrent required safeguarding action when abuse is suspected; the key does not supersede it.
A time-sensitive forensic examination is a specific form of the key's specialized assessment.
A limited non-leading history may be the immediate triage step while safety and referral remain simultaneously correct; repository evidence does not resolve sequencing.
Gestational trophoblastic disease can underlie severe pregnancy vomiting, so it may coexist with rather than replace hyperemesis gravidarum.
Maternal serum screening overlaps first-trimester combined screening; the stated correctness contexts do not separate them.
Correcting hypoxia or metabolic disturbance is a component of assessing and treating reversible causes.
Stopping a deliriogenic medication is a component of the key's reversible-cause response.
Chest-tube drainage with intrapleural therapy contains the key's pleural-drainage strategy and adds escalation therapy.
Other specified feeding or eating disorder is an umbrella that includes purging disorder and subthreshold bulimia presentations.
Asking permission and following the patient's lead substantially restates the key's patient-preference and self-determination action.

anchor_concerns: NEW-T18-PED-03 and NEW-T18-SURG-01 use compound keys, making component actions prone to containment or simultaneous correctness.
NEW-T18-PHELO-01 references remain usable only when the stem establishes an expressed patient preference.
NEW-T18-PHELO-03 actions are sequential; realized stems must establish capacity and decision stage.
NEW-T18-PED-01 stems must distinguish functional retention from organic causes.
cross_cutting_findings: All candidate feature profiles still need candidate-specific canonical evidence.
Pairwise admission must be derived from explicit candidate verdicts rather than blanket approval.
